newsitem.title: USA: Ariz. Navajo coal-fired unit 2 shut for repairs.
newsitem.headline: Ariz. Navajo coal-fired unit 2 shut for repairs.

text.p: A 750 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Navajo coal-fired generating station in Page, Ariz., was shut Tuesday to repair a boiler tube leak, sources familiar with the plant said Wednesday.
It is uncertain when the unit would resume operation, but some sources said the shutdown would likely be brief, and repairs would last until Thursday.
Navajo's other two 750 MW units were said to be operating normally.
The Navajo units are operated by Salt River Project, which also holds a 21.8 percent equity stake.
Other owners include the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, Los Angeles Department of Water and Power, Arizona Public Service Co, Nevada Power and Tucson Electric Power.
